title: Decoupling and Event-Driven Integration

header.html: Identify tightly and loosely coupled systems and decouple components (1.1.1); choose between synchronous and asynchronous patterns (1.1.2); implement event-driven patterns with EventBridge, S3 event notifications, SQS and SNS (1.1.8)
the official AWS Developer Associate (DVA-C03) exam guide, Task 1.1

html:
1Tight and loose coupling

Style What it means Risk or benefit
Tightly coupled A component calls another directly and waits; both must be up and fast One slow or failed part breaks the chain
Loosely coupled Components talk through a queue, topic or event bus; each can fail, scale and change on its own Absorbs spikes, hides failures, easier to change

AWS gives you three decoupling services: Amazon SQS (queue), Amazon SNS (publish and subscribe topic) and Amazon EventBridge (event bus with rules). AWS Step Functions coordinates multi-step workflows.

2Synchronous or asynchronous

Pattern Example Use when
Synchronous API Gateway calls Lambda; the client waits for the answer The caller needs the result now
Asynchronous with a queue App puts a message in SQS; a worker processes it later Spiky load, work can wait, you want retries
Asynchronous with events EventBridge routes an event to targets Many consumers react to a fact that happened
Exam tip

. "The user must see the result immediately" = synchronous. "Absorb traffic spikes" or "process later" = a queue.

3Amazon SQS

Feature Behavior
Standard queue At-least-once delivery, best-effort ordering, nearly unlimited throughput
FIFO queue Exactly-once processing, strict order within a message group ID
Visibility timeout After a consumer receives a message it is hidden for this time (default 30 seconds); if not deleted in time it reappears
Long polling WaitTimeSeconds up to 20 reduces empty responses and cost
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) Messages that fail maxReceiveCount times move here for study
Retention Default 4 days, up to 14 days

A consumer must delete a message after it succeeds. Make processing idempotent, because standard queues can deliver a message more than once. [Verify live] limits such as message size.

4Amazon SNS

SNS is publish and subscribe: one topic, many subscribers (SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email, SMS). Fan-out = publish once to SNS, deliver to several SQS queues. Subscription filter policies let each subscriber receive only the messages it needs.

5Amazon EventBridge and S3 events

Service Role
EventBridge Event bus that matches events with rules and event patterns and sends them to targets (Lambda, SQS, Step Functions and more); also scheduled rules and Scheduler
S3 Event Notifications S3 emits an event (object created, removed) to Lambda, SQS, SNS or EventBridge
Exam tip

. SNS = push to many. SQS = pull by one consumer group. EventBridge = route by content, many AWS and SaaS sources.

Exam tip

. Standard SQS can deliver a message more than once, so the consumer must be idempotent; FIFO is the choice for ordering and exactly-once processing.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A web app sends orders to a payment service that is sometimes slow, so the whole checkout fails. What change best decouples them?

  • AIncrease the web server instance size so it can wait longer for each payment response
  • BCall the payment service twice from the web server to improve the chance of success
  • CPut the orders on an Amazon SQS queue that the payment service reads
  • DStore the orders in the web server's memory until the payment service is ready
Show the answer

Answer: C. A queue absorbs the load and lets each side fail and scale on its own.

S2One upload to S3 must trigger a thumbnail Lambda, a metadata Lambda and an audit queue. Which design fits?

  • ACreate three S3 buckets and copy each upload into all of them with a script
  • BA cron job that lists the bucket every minute and starts the three consumers
  • CS3 event notification to an SNS topic with the three targets subscribed
  • DA single Lambda function that calls the other two and waits for both to finish
Show the answer

Answer: C. Fan-out through SNS delivers one event to many subscribers.

S3A consumer sometimes crashes after receiving a message and the message is processed twice. What should the developer do?

  • AShorten the retention period so duplicate messages expire sooner
  • BMake the processing idempotent and delete the message after success
  • CSwitch to a standard queue only and accept that duplicates cannot occur
  • DRemove the dead-letter queue so failed messages are never delivered again
Show the answer

Answer: B. At-least-once delivery means a message can arrive again, so processing must be idempotent.

S4Messages that always fail keep returning to the queue. Which feature isolates them for later study?

  • ALong polling
  • BA dead-letter queue
  • CA larger visibility timeout
  • DA FIFO queue
Show the answer

Answer: B. A DLQ receives messages that exceed maxReceiveCount.

S5An application must process orders in the exact order per customer and exactly once. Which queue type fits?

  • AStandard queue with one consumer per customer
  • BSNS topic with a subscription per customer
  • CFIFO queue with the customer ID as message group ID
  • DEventBridge bus with a rule per customer
Show the answer

Answer: C. FIFO preserves order within a message group and processes exactly once.

S6A team wants to route events from many AWS services by their content to different targets. Which service fits?

  • AAmazon SQS
  • BAmazon Kinesis Data Streams
  • CAWS CodePipeline
  • DAmazon EventBridge
Show the answer

Answer: D. EventBridge matches events against rules and event patterns and sends them to targets.

6.2 Recall questions

R1What is the default SQS visibility timeout?

Show the answer

30 seconds.

R2What does a FIFO queue guarantee?

Show the answer

Exactly-once processing and ordering within a message group ID.

R3What does long polling do?

Show the answer

It waits up to 20 seconds for messages, reducing empty responses and cost.

R4What is SNS fan-out?

Show the answer

Publishing once to a topic that delivers to several subscribers, often several SQS queues.

R5Name two targets of an S3 event notification.

Show the answer

For example Lambda, SQS, SNS or EventBridge.

R6Which services decouple application components?

Show the answer

SQS, SNS and EventBridge (with Step Functions for workflows).

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Coupling tight = direct call and wait; loose = queue, topic or bus
SQS standard (at-least-once) vs FIFO (exactly-once, ordered); visibility timeout; DLQ; long polling
SNS publish and subscribe, fan-out, filter policies
EventBridge rules and event patterns to targets
Idempotency required with at-least-once delivery
